poster_title: Search Self-play: Pushing the Frontier of Agent Capability without Supervision
authors: Hongliang Lu, Yuhang Wen, Pengyu Cheng, Ruijin Ding, Jiaqi Guo, Haotian Xu, Chutian Wang, Haonan Chen, Xiaoxi Jiang, Guanjun Jiang
paper_info: Alibaba, Peking University, Sun Yat-sen University, 2023

panels.headline: Addressing the scarcity of supervised training data in RLVR
content: RLVR is the mainstream technique for training LLM agents.
Training LLM agents is challenging due to the scarcity of supervised data.
Self-play methods have shown effectiveness in improving agent intelligence.
Proposes a scalable and self-sustaining method for generating high-quality question-answer pairs.
Reduces the demand for human-annotated verification while maintaining reward accuracy.

panels.headline: Proposer generates deep search queries with verifiable ground-truth and progressive difficulty
content: Designs a Search Self-play (SSP) game where the LLM plays two roles: a question proposer and a problem solver.
The proposer uses search tools to excavate implicit factual evidence and generates challenging search questions.
The solver attempts to answer the generated questions through multi-turn reasoning and search calling.
Uses retrieval-augmentation generation (RAG) to validate the correctness of each generated query.
panels.figure_caption: Examples of Search Self-play with a given ground-truth 'Dr. Will Boyd'.

panels.headline: Conducted experiments on various agentic benchmarks
content: Conducted experiments on various agentic benchmarks under both from-scratch and continual learning setups.
Compared the performance of SSP-trained agents against multiple strong open-source baselines.
panels.figure_caption: Ablation on training schemes. The complete search self-play ( +SSP ) significantly outperforms fixed-opponent variants.

panels.headline: SSP significantly improves search agents' performance
content: SSP significantly improves search agents' performance uniformly on various benchmarks.
Achieves improvements without any agentic data annotation or additional supervision.
Training dynamics show continuous improvement in search tool usage and response length.
panels.figure_caption: Training dynamics of SSP with Qwen2.5-7B-Base. (a) The agent learns to use the search tool more frequently. (b) Solver response length increases while prompt length remains stable. (c, d) Evaluation scores on both GeneralQA and Multi-HopQA datasets show continuous improvement during training.

panels.headline: Establishes a scalable pathway toward self-supervised agentic training
content: SSP establishes a scalable pathway toward self-supervised agentic training.
The method shows substantial and consistent improvements across various benchmarks.
The co-evolutionary dynamic between the proposer and solver is crucial for robust performance gains.
The effectiveness of the method is primarily demonstrated on deep search agents.
Future work could explore generalizing SSP to other types of LLM agents.
